subject: Post-demo model slate: prioritized candidates, deployment constraints & next steps

Subject: Post-demo model slate: prioritized candidates, deployment constraints & next steps

Hi Elena / Samir —

Thanks again for the demo time this morning. Quick recap and a recommended path forward based on what we heard about Innovexa's latency targets (<= 250ms p95), cost constraints for high-volume endpoints, and the need for high-fidelity summarization on long docs.

Attached: innovexa_benchmarks_20280129.csv (raw latency & quality sweep), innovexa_prompt_pack_v1.jsonl (example prompts + test sets), model_cost_estimates_q1.pdf (ballpark economics).

Top-line recommended slate (prioritized for a 2-week evaluation sprint):

1) Redwood-4b-ptq (candidate A) — balance pick
   - Why: best median latency at our baseline sequence lengths, strong recall on the summarization eval, very low inference cost after PTQ.
   - Tradeoffs: slightly lower factuality on very long-context (>8k) examples vs 13B; good fit for chat-style front-line endpoints.

2) OpenLlama-7B-int8 (candidate B) — cost-first fallback
   - Why: very competitive per-token cost, robust on instruction-following workloads, good throughput for batch inference.
   - Tradeoffs: higher p95 latency on single-request low-burst patterns; may need autoscale tuning or routing to a lower-latency variant for critical UI paths.

3) Redwood-13b-ptq (candidate C) — quality anchor
   - Why: highest scores on long-document cohesion and factuality in our benchmarks; recommended for the summarization API and any high-stakes outputs.
   - Tradeoffs: higher unit cost and latency; ideal as a canary/only-for-high-value routes or for offline batch summarization.

Suggested evaluation plan (2 weeks):
- Sprint week 1: run Redwood-4b-ptq and OpenLlama-7B-int8 against your prompt pack (we'll run the attached test harness).
- Sprint week 2: run Redwood-13b-ptq on a focused subset of the highest-risk prompts (3–5k tokens) and compare quality delta.
- Acceptance criteria: p95 latency <= 250ms for interactive endpoints (on dev region), ROUGE/QA pass rate improvement >= 8% when using 13B vs 4B for the target set, and cost per 1M tokens within the budget envelope you shared (~$45–$60).

Operational asks from your side:
- Please confirm which dataset we should use as the canonical eval sample (you can drop a link to Drive or share S3 creds — we will only use a read-only sample).
- Confirm whether the summarization route needs to be online only or if a hybrid online/batch approach is acceptable.
- Approve the 2-week evaluation sprint and the two primary candidates (A + B) to proceed.

If you confirm, we’ll provision evaluation endpoints in your region, kick off the harness, and send a short onboarding doc for authentication (we can use a temporary token).

Thanks — looking forward to your thoughts.

Best,

On Mon, Jan 29, 2028 at 10:15 AM Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com> wrote:
> Top-line recommended slate (prioritized for a 2-week evaluation sprint):
> 1) Redwood-4b-ptq (candidate A) — balance pick
> 2) OpenLlama-7B-int8 (candidate B) — cost-first fallback
> 3) Redwood-13b-ptq (candidate C) — quality anchor

Elena — quick numbers (rule-of-thumb estimates based on our January pricing and the configs in the attached econ PDF):
- Redwood-4b-ptq: ~$18–$22 per 1M tokens (inference only, excluding storage/transfer).
- OpenLlama-7B-int8: ~$12–$17 per 1M tokens (cheaper when batched; we saw good gains at >4 request batch).
- Redwood-13b-ptq: ~$48–$60 per 1M tokens (higher compute; still lower than full fp16 variants).

Fallback/routing pattern we recommend:
- Primary interactive route: Redwood-4b-ptq with aggressive KV/prefix caching and 50ms continuous-batching window disabled for UI calls (keeps single-request latency low).
- If p95 exceeds 250ms in a region, automatic fallback to OpenLlama-7B-int8 for non-critical responses (or switch to a smaller cached-template path).
- For very high-quality needs (billing summaries, legal copy), call Redwood-13b-ptq via an async job or a canary synchronous endpoint behind a confirmation step.

If helpful, we can produce a quick decision matrix that maps routes in your UI (chat primary, document analysis, export/reporting) to model variants + expected cost buckets.

— Ben

Perfect — thanks for the quick questions and for dropping the sample. Next concrete steps I propose: 

1) Confirm the eval dataset link (you said EOD, we’ll watch the Drive).
2) We provision two temporary evaluation endpoints for Redwood-4b-ptq and OpenLlama-7B-int8 in your us-west region and run the harness against the 2k sample. (ETA: 24–48 hours after dataset access).
3) Mid-sprint check-in (Day 7): we’ll share a short dashboard with p50/p95 latency, cost-to-date, and a quality delta table for the prompt pack.
4) End-of-sprint recommendation: choose whether to promote 4b as the primary interactive model with 13b reserved for high-fidelity routes, or to accept OpenLlama as the cheaper primary with 13b as fallback.

Operational notes: we’ll need a short-term token for the evaluation endpoints; if you prefer, we can provide a temporary OAuth client and scope-limited key. We will not store your full dataset beyond the evaluation sprint without explicit sign-off.

If that plan works, please reply with one-line confirmation and whether you prefer a token or OAuth for the harness.

Thanks — will stand up the endpoints once we have your confirmation and the Drive link.
